Empirical results are promising: gains are reported across CodeLlama and DeepSeek-Coder model scales, with deterministic gem5 timing, correctness filtering, and both BEST@1 and BEST@8 settings.

weaknesses: The central causal claim is under-controlled: PIE-Problem changes not only perspective but also speedup threshold, dataset size, problem coverage, target distribution, and prompting/training recipe. Matched ablations such as user-oriented pairs with the same 90% threshold, equal-size training sets, or cross-user pairs at comparable speedups are missing.

Evaluation is narrow, limited to C++ competitive-programming tasks from PIE/CodeNet. There is no external benchmark, real-world software optimization setting, other language, or direct assessment of transfer beyond this dataset family.

BEST@8 uses oracle selection by correctness tests and execution time, which may substantially inflate practical performance; the paper does not propose a realistic candidate selection or verification procedure.
The speedup reporting lacks uncertainty estimates, per-problem aggregation, medians, or robustness checks, so it is hard to know whether average speedup is driven by a small number of large wins.

Correctness is measured only by unit tests, while many generated outputs fail tests or compilation. The paper does not sufficiently address test-suite incompleteness or semantic equivalence risks for generated optimized programs.
Reproducibility details are incomplete: important hyperparameters, decoding limits, merge-weight selection protocol, validation usage, and release/link details are either absent or underspecified.

The model-merging contribution is useful but fairly ad hoc and not technically novel; comparisons to stronger execution-guided repair, search/reranking, retrieval, or problem-statement-aware baselines are missing.
The writing sometimes overclaims the contribution and contains clarity issues and typos, which weakens confidence in the framing despite the interesting empirical direction.

The baselines are incomplete for a top-tier claim: there is little comparison to retrieval, problem-statement-conditioned generation, stronger repair/verification loops, data filtering alternatives, or training on high-speedup user-oriented pairs.
Results lack uncertainty estimates, repeated seeds, per-problem distributions, or robustness checks; mean speedup can be dominated by outliers in performance-optimization benchmarks.
